cover.explanation: The body claims a fix for issue #3558 and the only changed surface (index 0) is internal docs and test data, so no non-internal surface needs judgment. The base-branch docs (docs/guide/cli.md line 497 and docs/api/lemonade.md, 'For llamacpp, with --no-mmap saved') document llamacpp_args as a passthrough of llama.cpp flags and show --no-mmap in their examples, but the pinned llama.cpp build (b10723 in backend_versions.json) marks --no-mmap 'DEPRECATED in favor of --load-mode' and warns at runtime, so updating the examples and test fixtures to --load-mode none — which yields the identical load mode — delivers the documented behavior with the currently supported flag. No server or CLI code is touched, so this introduces no new capability and the no-breaking-changes claim holds.

explanation.body: The title, body, and template claims describe what the diff does.
explanation.diff: The diff only edits docs and tests: docs/api/lemonade.md, docs/api/openai.md, and docs/guide/cli.md now show --load-mode none in llamacpp_args examples, and test/cpp/test_custom_args.cpp, test/cpp/test_hrx_contract.cpp, test/cpp/test_recipe_arg_resolution.cpp, and test/server_endpoints.py use --load-mode none instead of the deprecated --no-mmap. No lemonade server or CLI code is touched (base-branch src/cpp never referenced either flag), so saved options and runtime behavior for existing installs are unchanged. The body accurately describes the change and its no-breaking-changes claim holds.
explanation.quality: Checked docs/guide/cli.md, docs/api/lemonade.md, and docs/api/openai.md at the head SHA: the base branch had exactly nine --no-mmap references, all in those three pages, and a repo-wide case-insensitive grep of docs/ at head finds zero remaining mmap mentions, so no page is left untrue. The PR changes no source code; the changed tests (CustomArgsTest, RecipeArgResolutionTest, HrxContractTest via add_cpp_ci_test in CMakeLists.txt, and test/server_endpoints.py in cpp_server_build_test_release.yml) are pre-existing suites already wired into CI whose falsifiable assertions keep covering the untouched arg-resolution mechanism, so there is no behavioral surface that needs a new regression test.
